testName: IISER IAT - Alcohols, Phenols, and Ethers

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: What is the correct IUPAC name of the compound: CH3-CH(OH)-CH2-CH(CH3)-CH(CH3)2?
questions.explanation: Find the longest chain (6 carbons = hexan). Number from right to left to give -OH the lowest number (2). Substituents are methyls at C4 and C5. Name: 4,5-Dimethylhexan-2-ol.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The C-O-H bond angle in alcohols is slightly less than the tetrahedral angle (109.5°). Which of the following is the primary reason for this?
options: Resonance effect of the Oxygen atom.
Repulsion between the unshared electron pairs of Oxygen.
The high electronegativity of the Hydrogen atom.
The bulky nature of the alkyl group.
questions.explanation: According to VSEPR theory, lone pair-lone pair repulsion on the oxygen atom is stronger than bond pair-bond pair repulsion, causing the bond angle to decrease below 109.5°.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Arrange the following in increasing order of their boiling points: (I) Pentan-1-ol, (II) n-Butane, (III) Pentanal, (IV) Ethoxyethane.
questions.explanation: Boiling point order: Non-polar (Butane) < Weak polar (Ether) < Polar without H-bond (Aldehyde) < H-bonded (Alcohol).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: An organic compound with molecular formula C4H10O does not react with Sodium metal. Upon treatment with excess hot HI, it yields only one type of alkyl halide. The compound is:
questions.explanation: No reaction with Na means it is an ether. Yielding only one halide with excess HI implies it is a symmetrical ether. Diethyl ether (C2H5-O-C2H5) is the only symmetrical option.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: During the dehydration of alcohols to alkenes using concentrated H2SO4, the relative ease of dehydration follows the order:
options: All alcohols dehydrate at the same rate.
questions.explanation: Ease of dehydration depends on the stability of the intermediate carbocation (3° > 2° > 1°).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: When 3,3-dimethylbutan-2-ol is heated with concentrated H2SO4, the major product obtained is:
questions.explanation: The 2° carbocation formed initially undergoes a 1,2-methyl shift to form a more stable 3° carbocation. Deprotonation then gives 2,3-dimethylbut-2-ene.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which of the following reagents can be used to distinguish between Phenol and Benzyl alcohol?
questions.explanation: Phenols give a violet color with neutral FeCl3, whereas alcohols do not.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: In the reaction of Phenol with CHCl3 and aqueous NaOH (Reimer-Tiemann reaction), the electrophile involved is:
questions.explanation: The reaction generates dichlorocarbene (:CCl2) via alpha-elimination, which acts as the electrophile attacking the phenoxide ring.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Ortho-nitrophenol is more volatile than para-nitrophenol. This is due to:
options: Presence of intermolecular hydrogen bonding in ortho-isomer.
Presence of intramolecular hydrogen bonding in ortho-isomer.
Stronger inductive effect in the para-isomer.
questions.explanation: Intramolecular H-bonding in o-nitrophenol prevents it from associating with other molecules, making it steam-volatile.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Denatured alcohol is prepared by adding small amounts of:
questions.explanation: Methanol makes it toxic, and Pyridine gives it a foul smell, making the ethanol unfit for consumption.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: What is the chemical name of the side-product 'X' produced in the cumene process?
questions.explanation: Cumene hydroperoxide decomposes in acid to Phenol and Acetone.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The conversion of Cumene to Cumene hydroperoxide follows which mechanism?
questions.explanation: Aerial oxidation of cumene involves a radical chain reaction at the benzylic position.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: During the decomposition of cumene hydroperoxide with dilute acid, which group migrates to the electron-deficient oxygen atom?
questions.explanation: The phenyl group migrates from Carbon to Oxygen because of its higher migratory aptitude compared to methyl.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which of the following will not form Phenol when treated with aqueous NaOH at high temperature and pressure (Dow’s Process conditions)?
questions.explanation: 2,4-Dinitrochlorobenzene reacts with warm water/NaOH easily; it does not require the high temp/pressure of the Dow process.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Consider the reaction: CH3OC(CH3)3 + HI (excess) -> Products. The products formed are:
questions.explanation: Excess HI cleaves both sides of the ether. Tert-butyl methyl ether forms CH3I and (CH3)3CI.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Aspirin is obtained by the reaction of Salicylic acid with:
questions.explanation: Acetylation of the -OH group of salicylic acid with acetic anhydride produces Aspirin.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which of the following alcohols will react fastest with Lucas reagent?
questions.explanation: Tertiary alcohols react immediately with Lucas reagent via the SN1 mechanism.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Kolbe’s reaction of Sodium phenoxide with CO2 followed by acidification yields:
questions.explanation: Sodium phenoxide + CO2 -> Sodium salicylate -> Salicylic acid.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: What is the major product when Propan-1-ol is treated with Pyridinium Chlorochromate (PCC)?
questions.explanation: PCC oxidizes primary alcohols to aldehydes without further oxidation to acids.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Phenol is more acidic than Ethanol because:
options: Phenoxide ion is stabilized by resonance while ethoxide ion is not.
Phenol has a larger molecular weight.
Phenol is more soluble in water than ethanol.
The ethoxide ion is stabilized by the +I effect of the ethyl group.
questions.explanation: The phenoxide ion delocalizes the negative charge into the aromatic ring, significantly increasing its stability compared to the ethoxide ion.
